name: Rhinoceros 3D
tagline: General purpose NURBS surface and solid modeler used for industrial design, architecture, jewelry and marine design.

pricing.basis: one-time license, upgrade pricing for major versions
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Rhino is a geometry kernel with a UI bolted on, and the kernel is the product. Thirty years of work went into making NURBS trimming, filleting, booleans and surface intersection return answers that are both correct and tolerant of sloppy input, which is the part nobody one-shots. An agent can absolutely give you a local browser app that extrudes, lofts and booleans simple solids via OpenCASCADE WASM, and that is genuinely useful for brackets and enclosures. It will fall over the first time you ask for a variable-radius fillet on a trimmed freeform surface, or need a STEP file a machinist will accept. Add Grasshopper, the plugin ecosystem and the file format interop and the gap stops being a weekend and starts being a career.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser CAD scratchpad where you write parametric scripts against an OpenCASCADE WASM kernel, see the solid in a three.js viewport, and export STEP or STL.
requirements: Node 20+ and a browser with WebAssembly
willingness to model by writing code instead of clicking
a slicer or CAM tool downstream, since this exports only
whatYouLose: A NURBS kernel that survives messy geometry: trims, blends, variable fillets, surface intersections that do not silently fail
Grasshopper, which for many users is the actual reason they bought Rhino
The plugin ecosystem: rendering, jewelry, marine, structural, nesting, all third party and all assuming Rhino
Real file interop with IGES, STEP, DWG, SAT, 3DM and the twenty other formats clients send you
2D drafting, dimensions, layouts and printable drawings, which is half of professional CAD work
moatNotes: The moat is numerical robustness, which is invisible until it is missing, and then it is the only thing you notice.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a perpetual license costs less than a week of billable time and the alternative is geometry that fails at 2am before a deadline. People also pay for the ecosystem: Grasshopper definitions, plugins, tutorials, and the fact that every collaborator and fabricator in their industry already reads 3DM. A code-first personal modeler is a fine toy and a decent parts generator, but it is not something you hand a client.
notes: A scripted solid modeler on top of OpenCASCADE is a real weekend project and worth doing. The moat is a battle-hardened NURBS kernel plus Grasshopper and every plugin author who built against it.
prompt:
Build a local, offline parametric CAD scratchpad. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + TypeScript, replicad (which wraps OpenCASCADE via WASM) for geometry, three.js for the viewport, CodeMirror 6 for the editor. Everything runs in the browser from a static build. No backend.

Layout: single page, editor on the left, 3D viewport on the right, console strip along the bottom.

In scope:
- The editor holds a TypeScript-ish script that is evaluated in a Web Worker and returns one or more replicad shapes.
- Expose a small modeling API in the worker scope: sketch primitives (rect, circle, polyline, bezier), extrude, revolve, loft, sweep, offset, shell, boolean union/subtract/intersect, fillet and chamfer by edge selection filters.
- A parameters block at the top of the script, declared as a plain exported object of named numbers, is parsed and rendered as sliders and number inputs. Dragging a slider re-runs the script and re-renders. Debounce re-runs to 150ms.
- Tessellate the resulting shapes and render them with flat-shaded faces plus dark edge overlay. Orbit, pan, zoom. Grid and axes. Orthographic toggle.
- Export buttons: STEP and STL, both produced by OpenCASCADE, downloaded as files.
- Scripts persist in localStorage with a named list, plus import and export of a single .json project file.
- Geometry errors from the kernel get caught and printed to the console strip with the script line number if available. Never leave the viewport showing stale geometry after a failed run without saying so.
- Ship 4 example scripts: a parametric enclosure with a lid, a flanged pipe, a bracket with counterbored holes, a lofted handle.

Out of scope, do not build: interactive mouse-driven sketching, constraint solver, assemblies, 2D drawing output, dimensions, rendering or materials, any file format other than STEP and STL, multi user anything.

Performance: load the OpenCASCADE WASM once in the worker and keep it warm. Show a spinner on first load. Keep the main thread free during rebuilds.

Deliver a README with install, dev and build commands, a one page description of the modeling API, and a blunt Limitations section that says this is not a replacement for a production NURBS modeler and names what will break first: complex trims, variable fillets, imported geometry repair.
